result.shard_summary: A homelab GPU/LLM benchmarking + monkey-patch toolkit: benchmark probes and pinned-source build scripts are genuinely rigorous (tree-hash verification, contamination flags, steady-state decode math), while the vllm-xpu side is a tower of four independent exact-string patchers over installed site-packages that will all break silently-or-loudly on every image upgrade. Overall health: good measurement engineering, fragile delivery mechanism.

module_verdicts.rationale: Sound harness: fresh git fixture per task, hidden check.sh, verify mode with reference patch. Real isolation-by-construction, not theater.

Does isolate the filesystem (only $QWEN_CWD mounted, throwaway HOME) but --network=host plus skipped permissions makes the network boundary nonexistent; fine for a trusted homelab, misnamed as a sandbox.
Small live probe, real assertions on real server responses; only flaw is it cannot be used as a gate because it always exits 0.
Careful phase design, cpuset restore on EXIT trap, guard against serving-cpu-guard interference. stress() launch failure is unchecked.
Correct decode-only methodology (prefill each slot, then timed pass); uncached-token leak indicator is honest measurement hygiene.

The steady-overlap-window computation (lines 83-87) is genuinely good benchmarking; but it is a second implementation of decode-streams.py with a different config surface (env vars vs argparse) and crashes on servers that omit usage.
Solid short measurement set with real usage validation and shared-server idle gate; module-level execution and model-specific TOK_PER_WORD constant are the only warts.
The counter-delta contamination check (line 23) is real diligence, but the pipeline is glued by sed-regex over another script's prose output.
Pinned base commit + patch series + git tree-hash verification is exactly how benchmark binary provenance should be done.
~90 percent duplicate of llama.cpp-sycl/build.sh with only BASE/TREE/FETCH/targets differing; two builders will drift.
module_verdicts.salvage_note: Salvage the case-style variant table (lines 18-30: BASE/FETCH/TREE/DIR per build flavor) into one parameterized build.sh taking a variant name; delete the copy.

module_verdicts.rationale: Digest-pinned container, sane log-on-fail; small and honest.
Appropriate regex parse of a debug trace format that is itself line-oriented; correct diff and counter rollup.
Device-by-PCI-path selection is the right OS boundary; unquoted $OUT/$CR/$RR paths are the only bug.
Clean offline vocabulary builder with honest held-out coverage reporting across K values.

The idea (score only draft-vocab rows, -inf elsewhere, target verifies full head so correctness is preserved) is excellent; the delivery vehicle (exact-string replace into site-packages) is an upgrade landmine.
module_verdicts.salvage_note: Keep the generated compute_logits/get_top_tokens/_draft_vocab_ids block (lines 29-59) as a patch file in a git fork or a sitecustomize import hook applied at container build; delete the self-rewriting patcher pattern.

module_verdicts.rationale: One-line jinja mapping fixing a real 400-failure class; guarded by count check. Still a prose-string patcher that dies silently when the template changes.
module_verdicts.salvage_note: Keep the effort-word mapping (high/max->xhigh, minimal/none->low, null->default) as a checked-in .jinja overlay in the image build; delete the runtime patcher.

module_verdicts.rationale: Correct correctness-critical fix (length stop must not masquerade as tool_calls) with clever upstream-fix detection, but delivered as a second independent string-patcher against the same site-packages tree.
module_verdicts.salvage_note: Keep the (old,new,upstream) hunk triple with upstream-supersession detection (lines 25-42) and carry it as a quilt/git patch series in the image Dockerfile; delete the bespoke patcher.

module_verdicts.rationale: Pragmatic pytest-free differential runner; fake pytest skip raising RuntimeError is hacky but honest.
Correct mechanism (systemd slice AllowedCPUs + container cpuset, restore-on-stop) at the right OS boundary; polling loop treats fetch failure as idle.

The schema-validation fallback ladder (constrain name only, then no constraint, never a 500) is real defensive engineering; the appended code references unasserted module globals and joins the same patcher tower.
module_verdicts.salvage_note: Keep _strict_tools_tag with its per-schema cache and fail-soft ladder (lines 59-99) as a proper upstream PR or fork patch; the reference to ChatCompletionToolsParam/FunctionTool/get_model_structural_tag must be asserted like the other anchors.

module_verdicts.rationale: Clear first-fit banking planner with honest CPU-leftover reporting; t.shape[2] expert-count assumption is brittle against 2D tensors.

findings.title: Four independent exact-string monkey-patchers over one site-packages tree
findings.mechanism: draft-vocab.py, effort-template.py, length-finish.py and strict-tools.py each read installed vLLM/jinja sources, assert on a hardcoded prose snippet, and rewrite the file in place with a .orig backup. Any image upgrade shifts the anchor text and every patcher asserts out at deploy time, or worse applies over a partially changed file; there is no inventory of which patches a running image carries and no ordering guarantee between them.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Replace all four with one git fork of the pinned llm-scaler tree carrying the hunks as a numbered patch series applied by the image Dockerfile (the same pattern llama.cpp-sycl/build.sh already proves with tree-hash verification); emit the patched tree hash into the server log for provenance.

findings.title: Sandbox with --network=host and skipped permissions
findings.mechanism: The script claims the working copy is the only host path the agent sees, but --network=host plus --dangerously-skip-permissions lets the evaluated agent reach every host-local service (including the QWEN_PROXY backend and anything on localhost) and exec freely; a prompt-injected fixture repo can exfiltrate or pivot.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Drop --network=host, add -p 127.0.0.1::8399 style port mapping or --network with only the proxy reachable, and keep permissions skipped only inside a user-namespaced container (--security-opt no-new-privileges, read-only rootfs).

findings.title: Fail-open constraint drop on any xgrammar exception
findings.mechanism: valid() catches bare Exception and returns False, and _STRICT_TAG_OK False means the request proceeds with no grammar at all — exactly the unconstrained mode that once emitted a tool named Bash-backtick. A malformed or adversarial tool schema in a request therefore silently disables the guard the patch exists to provide.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Make the combined-tag failure configurable: fail closed (reject request) when VLLM_STRICT_TOOLS_MODE=strict, and always log the dropped schema hash so silent constraint loss is observable in metrics.

findings.title: Appended patch code references unasserted module globals
findings.mechanism: The appended block uses ChatCompletionToolsParam, FunctionTool and get_model_structural_tag at call time; unlike the anchor assertions above, their presence is never checked, so an upstream rename turns every auto tool request into a NameError 500 — the exact failure mode the patch documents avoiding.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Add assert lines for each referenced symbol in the host source before appending, same as the existing s.count checks, so a rename fails at patch time not at request time.

findings.title: Benchmark pipeline glued by sed over another script's prose output
findings.mechanism: spec-step-cost.sh extracts the decode rate by sed-matching the literal phrase `decode aggregate <num> tok/s` from decode-vllm.py's formatted print line; any wording or format change in decode-vllm.py silently yields an empty rate, and awk then divides by zero-ish r and prints garbage step-ms numbers with no error.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Make decode-vllm.py emit a machine-readable line (jsonl to stderr or a --json flag) and have spec-step-cost.sh consume that; or have decode-vllm.py itself read the spec-decode counters and print steps/ms, deleting the wrapper entirely.

findings.title: Probe prints OK/WRONG verdicts but always exits 0
findings.mechanism: All four checks report correctness only via stdout strings; any wrapper (CI, cron, health gate) sees exit 0 whether the server's constrained decoding is broken or not, so the probe cannot actually gate anything.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Accumulate failures in a list and sys.exit(1 if failures else 0) at the end; also catch json/KeyError per check so one malformed response reports WRONG instead of crashing before the other checks run.

findings.title: Unguarded usage indexing crashes the whole benchmark run
findings.mechanism: If any stream's final usage chunk is missing or usage stays None (proxy hiccup, server restart, timeout mid-stream), usage.get(...) raises TypeError / usage[completion_tokens] raises KeyError, killing all threads and discarding every completed row of a multi-minute run.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Wrap the return-dict construction: if usage is None or lacks completion_tokens, return a sentinel row and have the caller report and skip that stream instead of propagating.

findings.title: Dual config surfaces for twin benchmark scripts
findings.mechanism: decode-streams.py takes argparse flags (--streams, --chars, --tokens) while decode-vllm.py, its declared mirror, reads env vars STREAMS/CHARS/TOKENS and positional argv with no argparse; users must remember two incompatible invocations for the same experiment matrix.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Extract the shared prompt-construction/matrix-iteration into one module, give both frontends (or one frontend with --backend llama|vllm) the same argparse interface.

findings.title: Metrics fetch failure is indistinguishable from idle
findings.mechanism: busy() pipes curl output into awk; if every curl fails (server container restarting, port down, metrics endpoint hung beyond -m 1), awk sums nothing and exits 0 = idle, so the guard opens the CPUs to user load while the server is actually mid-crash-loop or rebooting into a serving state; conversely a hung poll never escalates.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Track per-port fetch success: if all curls returned empty/non-200, keep the current split state and log a warning instead of decoding it as idle; alert after N consecutive failures.

findings.title: Append-only results and last-stdout-line JSON make reruns ambiguous
findings.mechanism: run() opens the out jsonl in append mode, so re-running a label mixes stale rows from earlier code/models into the same file with no way to distinguish epochs; agent telemetry comes from json.loads of the final stdout line, which silently becomes {} (nulls in every column) whenever the agent prints a trailing non-JSON line.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Write to a timestamped file or truncate per (label, run-id) recorded in each row; on JSON parse failure record raw[-300:] in the row so the failure is inspectable instead of silently null.

findings.title: stress() never checks the transient unit actually started
findings.mechanism: systemd-run failure (unit name collision from $$-$RANDOM, stress-ng missing, scope limit) leaves STRESS set but nothing running; the phase then measures idle CPU while labeling it busy/pinned, producing confidently wrong contention numbers — the worst outcome for a measurement script.
findings.fix_or_replacement: After systemd-run, poll systemctl --user is-active $STRESS (up to ~5s) and abort the phase with an error if the unit is not active; also verify taskset/stress-ng exist upfront.

result.shard_summary: A 2,668-line monolithic build script that hand-folds ~15 untyped dict 'tables' (types, models, boxes, engines, checks, bench, batch, window) into data.json for a viz page, executing nearly everything at module scope. The measurement-provenance discipline (tag/src/evidence on every value) is genuinely good, but it is undermined by exec()-based plugin loading, regex-against-prose 'verification' of engine behavior and sanity, post-hoc retrojection of maintained intent onto recorded runs, and silent subsystem vanishing when ledger rows are absent.

module_verdicts.rationale: The core evidence-table pipeline (n(), evidence_of, hdr_summary, heat loading, bench least-squares fits) earns its keep and is structurally load-bearing for the whole page. But the plugin exec(), the regex sanity/flag theater, and the maintained-intent retrojection are negative-value subsystems that must be ripped or replaced with structural boundaries, and the module-scope side-effect sprawl makes the file untestable as constructed.

findings.title: exec() of families/*.py into build globals()
findings.mechanism: Every .py file in families/ is compiled and exec'd in the module globals with zero isolation: any file there gets arbitrary code execution, full write access to models/engines/checks/FAMILY_QUALITY, and can shadow any name the build later uses. A typo'd family file corrupts unrelated tables silently because it mutates shared global dicts.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Replace with a typed entry point: each family file defines build_family(ctx) returning a plain dataclass/dict; build.py calls it explicitly and merges under validation (same overlay.py rules as data/*.json). No exec, no globals injection.

findings.title: Engine sanity 'verified' by regexing the number 391 in a prose note
findings.mechanism: window_attempts decides an attempt passed engine sanity via re.search(r'sanity[^;]*391', layout_note): a hardcoded magic token count scraped from free-text notes. Anything else in the note (or a different count) reads as False/None; the note author controls the 'verification'. This is a rubber stamp dressed as a READ-tagged measurement.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Delete the sanity field entirely, or have record_* tools write an explicit structured boolean (sanity_pass: true, count) at capture time; never re-derive ground truth from prose.

findings.title: fallback/expert_residency 'controls' are regexes over engine-flag strings
findings.mechanism: checks.fallback.controls and expert_residency.controls 'enforce' engine behavior by matching patterns like --dspark[ =]+auto, --ssd-cache 0, layer split (\d[\d,]*) against recipe.conditions.engine_flags strings. A recipe that sets the flag differently, wraps it in a script, or lies in conditions passes; nothing observes the live engine. The src even admits 'no SHEXP/HC positive dispatch receipt exists here'.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Keep the pattern tables only as ledger-descriptive metadata; move enforcement to the run-capture path where the launcher emits a machine-readable flag struct (parsed argv, not regex on a string) recorded before launch.

findings.title: maintained_recipe_checks retrojects today's intent onto recorded runs
findings.mechanism: Historical ledger rows get a fallback_plan injected from current recipes/*.json spec files, keyed only on id/box/model/engine equality, producing a hybrid row that is neither the captured launch nor the maintained recipe. Downstream check evaluation cannot distinguish 'the run was safe' from 'we wish it had been', inviting accuracy-report contamination even with the basis label.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Evaluate maintained checks only in a separate prospective table joined at report time by recipe id; never mutate the run rows. The compatibility-guard idea (lines 1428-1429) is worth keeping as a join predicate.

findings.title: Per-card expert placement parsed from run-label prose
findings.mechanism: placements for lassie-orn35 runs are reconstructed by a human reading ledger labels ('10 on the GTX 1080 Ti (blk 0-8 + 10...)') and hardcoding layer lists, with o2 marked ESTIMATE by copying o6's split. Any future run whose placement lives in its label is invisible to predictRecipe; the o2 guess can be wrong by the blk.40 difference the comment itself flags.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Add a structured placement field to record_run.py intake and backfill these three rows once; delete the prose-derived table.

findings.title: Module-scope side-effect sprawl: sys.path mutation, importlib exec, file reads at import
findings.mechanism: The module imports heatmap via sys.path.insert, executes heat_shape.py/overlay.py/window_inputs.py via spec/loader, reads a dozen JSON files, mutates HEAT_USED/models/checks, and defines CLI behavior (--calibration-data-sha256) all at top level in interleaved order. Nothing is importable for testing, import order is load-bearing (heat_sets before extra_heat_sets), and one missing file mid-file leaves half-built globals.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Wrap in a main() that constructs tables in explicit stages via plain imports of the sibling modules (they are local packages; make tools/ and probe/ importable properly), so a failure is atomic and each stage is unit-testable.

findings.title: O(N^2)+ row rescans in gpu_stacks/gpu_lines
findings.mechanism: gpu_stacks re-filters all rows per backend, then per stack calls gpu_lines which re-filters ok rows again per backend and per (box,gpu) inside nested comprehensions; row_stack is recomputed per comparison (json.dumps per row per stack key). With a growing bench ledger this is quadratic-plus in row count on every build.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Group rows once into a dict keyed by (backend, box, gpu_id, stack-json) before fitting; compute row_stack one time per row and cache it.

findings.title: fnxc = shallow dict(models['fnx']) shares all nested mutable state
findings.mechanism: models['fnxc'] = dict(models['fnx']) copies one level: lookups, draft, row_limits, host_engine, and the later-added kv_host are the same dict objects as fnx. A subsequent in-place mutation of either model's shared subtree (the file's dominant idiom) silently corrupts the other; only the explicitly .update()d keys diverge.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Use copy.deepcopy (already imported) for the base, or define fnxc from a shared build_model() constructor taking the divergent fields.

findings.title: batch term depends on overlay-injected 'hand' key and silently vanishes on missing rows
findings.mechanism: card_vram_gib reads _bgpu['vram_gib']['hand'], a key that only exists after probe/overlay.py rewrites the n() dict; under FITVIZ_OVERLAYS=0 (the documented hand-tables-only mode) this KeyErrors mid-build. Conversely, any missing BATCH_ROWS ledger entry only prints and then sets batch=None, so the whole batched-decode section disappears from data.json without a non-zero exit.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Read vram_gib['v'] with a fallback to the hand value; make missing mandatory ledger rows a hard build error (or an explicit --allow-missing flag) instead of print-plus-None.

findings.title: Non-atomic snapshot rewrite into tracked src/ during build
findings.mechanism: input_path copies live sources over src/inputs snapshots with shutil.copyfile directly at the destination: an interrupted build leaves a truncated snapshot that a later commit carries as truth, and a concurrent build reading the same snapshot sees a torn file. Path components come from fitviz.local.json dirs config with no confinement.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Write to snap.tmp then os.replace for atomicity, and validate that resolved live paths stay inside the configured source roots.

result.shard_summary: A 2,668-line single-namespace Python build script, a 1,005-line monolithic Node CLI, and two family-plugin scripts executed inside the build's global namespace. Genuine, unusually rigorous validation work (cross-checking specs against headers, honest ESTIMATE/UNKNOWN tagging) is undermined by regex-archaeology over free-text notes, substring-based evidence attribution, exec() of sibling code, and a dual-language (Python/Node) calibration-hash ritual that spawns a synchronous python3 process per check.

module_verdicts.rationale: The validation core (window_config split coverage, ubench/spec layer-kind clash checks, priors completeness) is real invariant enforcement, not theater. But exec() of priors_adapter.py, double data.json serialization, substring run-id attribution, and regex extraction of 'MEASURED' numbers from layout_note prose are structural defects needing surgical fixes.
module_verdicts.salvage_note: page_assignment_parts (lines 2597-2622): clean recursive size-bounded statement splitting with an indivisible-scalar guard; keep as-is, it is the best code in the shard.

module_verdicts.rationale: Fifteen subcommands in one early-exit chain is ugly but functional and each branch does real work with honest labeling (post-hoc vs launch, replayed vs frozen). Fix the synchronous python3 spawn, hostname-gated symlink resolution, and the unbounded knob-combo cartesian solve; do not rewrite.
module_verdicts.salvage_note: Lines 96-103 and 2508 (EVIDENCE_CITE_MIN) honesty framing ('not judged, so not passed', 'GO never covers them') is a discipline worth preserving verbatim in any refactor.

module_verdicts.rationale: Every borrowed number is explicitly tagged ESTIMATE with the analog run cited (acceptance 0.85 'the low end', GLM-scaled compute buffer with the derivation shown) -- the opposite of cosplay. Defect is architectural: it runs in build.py's bare namespace with ~20 implicit globals (n, R, E, models, kldglm, KQM_TY, FNXH, ...) and fabricates one provenance string via FNXH.replace().
module_verdicts.salvage_note: Lines 56-62 (Gated DeltaNet state-size arithmetic: full-attention KV + f32 recurrent/conv state derivation) are a clean, reusable VRAM model for hybrid-attention families; extract into a shared helper both family files call.

module_verdicts.rationale: Honest UNKNOWN/ESTIMATE tagging throughout (mult_default 1.0 'neutral placeholder, not an acceptance claim'), but copy.deepcopy(models['orn122']) then dict-patch inheritance creates a silent load-order dependency on orn122.py having executed first (uses GG, ORN_CTX, GLM_CB4096_MIB, models['orn122']) with zero enforcement -- a KeyError away from a confusing build failure.
module_verdicts.salvage_note: Lines 34-38 (explicitly refusing to inherit the 122B's shapes/evidence while borrowing only numerical priors) document the right inheritance boundary; keep the pattern, enforce it with an explicit context object.

findings.title: exec() of sibling file in build namespace
findings.mechanism: exec(open('src/priors_adapter.py').read()) runs arbitrary code with full access to every build global (models, data, ledger); any planted or corrupted sibling file silently mutates the entire planner dataset before it is hashed and frozen, and the calibration identity then certifies the tampered output as FROZEN.
findings.fix_or_replacement: importlib.util.spec_from_file_location + a module exposing apply_priors(data); the same pattern build.py already uses for tps/build_tps.py at line 2662.

findings.title: Dual-language canonicalization: python3 subprocess per --check
findings.mechanism: Because JS and Python serialize floats/JSON differently, the calibration check spawns execFileSync('python3', ['build.py', '--calibration-data-sha256']) on every --check invocation, shipping the entire data.json over stdin to recompute a hash Python could have written into meta at build time. A 300-line frozen-manifest ritual exists to paper over the fact that there is no single canonicalization owner across the language boundary.
findings.fix_or_replacement: build.py writes data_sha256 into data.json meta.calibration at build time (it already computes it at line 2590); report.js hashes the raw data.json bytes it already read (storedData) and compares -- zero subprocesses, one owner.

findings.title: 'MEASURED' stage-window numbers regex-harvested from free-text notes
findings.mechanism: curve_configs parses engine flags with per-field user-supplied regexes over a concatenated flag string, then win_re.findall() scrapes stage timings out of recipe.layout_note prose (line 2310). A note reading 'stage run n=8 ... 41.02 ms' yields a number tagged MEASURED and fed to the fit; a reworded note silently yields no window term at all -- no error, just absent data.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Move stage timings into a structured measured.stage_ms field on the ledger row (record_run.py already writes measured dicts); keep the regex only as a loud deprecation path that prints 'row X: layout_note timings no longer parsed'.

findings.title: Evidence attribution by substring run-id match
findings.mechanism: stamp_evidence links a value to ledger runs via `i in src or any(s in src for s in ss)` -- plain substring containment between run ids and source prose, gated only by EVIDENCE_CITE_MIN=12 (line 2508), a magic length below which a source 'names no one run'. A run id appearing incidentally in any source string fabricates a citation; a cited run whose id is short is silently dropped.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Have ledger rows cite run ids in an explicit runs: [...] array field and match on exact set membership; drop the 12-char threshold entirely.

findings.title: Exhaustive 384-combo cartesian knob search with full solver per cell
findings.mechanism: rec() enumerates 2*3*2*2*2*2*2 = 384 knob combos, then for each of 2 models x N boxes x M engines runs a full FM.prepare/frontier/bestAt solve; combined with the frontier block at lines 918-933 (boxes x 3 knobsets x 4 models x 2 modes x engines) this is hundreds to thousands of independent solver invocations, each reconstructing FM.context from scratch with no memoization across combos sharing a prefix.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Prune in rec() itself (the skip conditions at lines 972-976 are evaluated only after full enumeration) and memoize FM.context per (bk,mk,eng) since knobs like addOptane/freeDesktop only alter capacities -- or cache prepare() results keyed on the effective context inputs.

findings.title: Provenance string fabricated via .replace() on another family's source text
findings.mechanism: The heat-set src is built as FNXH.replace('Flash-Next routing not counted yet (scout measurement 3 counts it)', 'Ornith routing not counted yet: UNKNOWN routing') -- string surgery on the Flash-Next family's evidence citation produces a src that cites Flash-Next's provenance chain for Ornith's synthetic heat, misattributing where the shape came from.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Write the Ornith src string directly ('synthetic GLM shape, seed=122, no Ornith routing counts'); the FNXH replace saves 3 lines at the cost of a false citation trail.

findings.title: deepcopy-then-patch inheritance with implicit load-order coupling
findings.mechanism: o35 = copy.deepcopy(models['orn122']) then .update()/draft.update() patches: orn35 silently requires orn122.py to have exec'd first (GG module, ORN_CTX, GLM_CB4096_MIB, GLM_VOCAB, models['orn122'], KQM_TY all implicit build globals). Any field orn122 later adds or renames (e.g. draft structure change) half-propagates: stale fields survive the patch as orphaned 122B numbers in the 35B entry.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Replace both family files' run-in-build-namespace contract with an explicit loader: build.py calls family.register(ctx) where ctx exposes models/types/helpers as an object; orn35 composes from orn122's register output via an explicit field list, not deepcopy.

findings.title: data.json serialized and written twice
findings.mechanism: json.dump(data...) at line 2551, then planner_outputs() runs node (up to 300 s), three blocks are grafted on, and the entire data tree is re-serialized and rewritten at line 2591. For a multi-MB document this doubles serialization cost and leaves a window where a crash leaves the first, calibration-less data.json on disk looking valid.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Write once after planner_outputs grafts; if the pre-advisor dump is deliberately sacrificial, delete line 2551 and document why.

findings.title: Hostname string match gates symlink resolution
findings.mechanism: os.hostname().split('.')[0] === r.box decides whether paths are realpathSync'd; a box whose hostname differs from the recipe's box key (containers, aliases, FQDN with different short name) silently skips resolution and the check runs on unexpanded paths, and realpathSync failures are swallowed to return the raw path with no note.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Pass an explicit --on-box flag or per-box fact from data.boxes (box hostname recorded at intake) instead of inferring locality from hostname; on resolve failure emit a res.checks note, not silence.

findings.title: Sync git subprocess with null-swallowing in --predict provenance capture
findings.mechanism: git(...) wraps execFileSync in try/catch returning null, so a repo without git (or a git failure) records rm_commit: null and rm_dirty: false -- the false reads as a clean tree in the prediction record, the exact opposite of the unknown state. The record is then frozen as pre-run provenance.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Distinguish the three states: return {commit, dirty: true|false|undefined} and refuse --predict outright when commit is unavailable, since a provenance record with no provenance is theater.

findings.title: Dynamic import of tps/build_tps.py shares build globals by side effect
findings.mechanism: exec_module of build_tps runs with no arguments contract beyond write(HERE, data, PAGE_DIR); like the family files, it executes against whatever module state exists at line 2664, and a failure inside it aborts the build after data.json and page/ were already written -- a partially published tree with no rollback.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Wrap in try/except that logs and exits nonzero BEFORE any writes complete, or write all outputs to a staging dir and rename atomically at the end; the latter also fixes the double-write window.

result.shard_summary: A read-only Linux hardware/model-header probing suite that mostly does what it claims: tagged READ/MEASURED values with provenance, honest UNKNOWNs, header-only model intake. It is unusually healthy, but suffers duplicated GPU-matching/diff logic across overlay.py and probe_box.py, a regex tower over prose benchmark logs in window_inputs.py, silent GPU drops in the xpu parser, non-atomic state writes, and an optional vitals_adapter that adds near-zero value.

module_verdicts.rationale: Genuinely read-only, careful collector: unset of shadowed shell functions, sudo -n only, @@!section failure markers, space-quoting via tr. Structurally sound; only minor fragilities in its ad-hoc KV line format.
Clean stdlib GGUF header reader with a sound chunked Reader, offset-derived tensor sizes (type-independent), shard expansion. Minor: GGML_TYPES table is dead weight since sizes never depend on names.

Real range-request header intake from HF/safetensors/GGUF/ssh with tag discipline. Needs surgical fixes: HF-token redirect handling, atomic --write, and the giant CLASSES regex ladder is a maintenance hazard but earns its keep for now.

Rank-based merge over untyped dicts is a hand-rolled fold with a duplicate GPU matcher (vs probe_box.match_gpus), a 'hand' key namespace that collides with real keys, and silent positional GPU fallback. Replace the merge with a single typed schema + one canonical matcher.
module_verdicts.salvage_note: Keep the RANK (MEASURED>READ>FIT>UNKNOWN) tag lattice and the audit log of add/replace/conflict; put them in one merge function parameterized by a typed field spec.

module_verdicts.rationale: The core probe is honest (tagged values, unknown registry, resolver for btrfs/loop/dm chains). Fix: silent xpu JSON drops, non-atomic --write, brittle PCI-substring GPU matching, and the duplicated match_gpus/_gpu_match/diff logic.

An optional, stale-prone, annotate-only cross-check that can never change a value, duplicates the disk-kind taxonomy with a weaker one ('image' auto-agrees with everything), and is wired in via except ImportError: pass. Pure optional weight; the probe is self-sufficient per its own docstring.

Regex tower over human-formatted STAGE ROLL-UP prose (column counts guessed as `cols[2:] if x.isdigit()`, table end detected by a heuristic break, kind attribution by name-substring tiebreak). Any whitespace change in the upstream tool silently mis-parses numbers.
module_verdicts.salvage_note: Keep parse_spec (lines 24-40): a clean 15-line dims/layer line format. Replace parse_ubench by making the XeStrata ubench tool emit JSON (its own --json flag) — one wire boundary instead of 90 lines of prose scraping.

findings.title: Duplicate GPU matcher with silent positional fallback cross-assignment
findings.mechanism: _gpu_match is a near-copy of probe_box.match_gpus (lines 600-615); both fall back to assigning leftover probed GPUs to unmatched hand slots by list order, so on a rebussed box a hand entry silently absorbs a different physical card's VRAM/driver data with only a generic 'replace' log line.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Delete both copies; one match_by_pci(hand, probed) that matches only on exact PCI (hand 'pci' key or parsed short address) and reports unmatched probed GPUs as gpus_unlisted without positional backfill.

findings.title: Microbenchmark cost model fed by prose-regex table scraping
findings.mechanism: parse_ubench reconstructs a numeric table from whitespace-split tokens: the row grid is guessed as `cols[2:] if x.isdigit()`, ntail is derived from that guess, table termination depends on `if classes and (totals or unmeasured): break`, and class-to-kind attribution falls back to a case-insensitive name-substring (class_kind lines 101-112). A renamed column or an extra footnote line shifts every parsed float into the wrong field with no error.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Make batch_window_ubench emit a machine-readable summary (JSON or CSV with a header contract); this file then reduces to parse_spec plus a json.load of that output.

findings.title: HF_TOKEN sent via urllib redirects outside huggingface.co
findings.mechanism: The Authorization header is set only for huggingface.co hostnames, but resolve URLs 302/302 to CDN hosts (cas-bridge.xethub.hf.co, cdn-lfs); urllib.request follows redirects and re-sends request headers, leaking the bearer token to third-party CDN hosts on older Pythons and to any host a repo can redirect to.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Use a custom HTTPRedirectHandler that strips the Authorization header on any cross-host redirect (or open with an opener that pins credentials per-URL), and assert the final URL host is *.hf.co / *.huggingface.co before sending the token.

findings.title: Non-atomic --write truncates data files on crash
findings.mechanism: `open(a.write, 'w').write(js)` truncates data/models/KEY.json in place; a crash, full disk, or Ctrl-C mid-write destroys the previous good entry (the same pattern at probe_box.py:718-720 and header_out at :399).
findings.fix_or_replacement: Write to a temp file in the same directory and os.replace() it; one 3-line helper shared by all three call sites.

findings.title: parse_xpu silently drops GPUs on JSON decode failure
findings.mechanism: `except ValueError: continue` discards an xpu-smi device record wholesale; a truncated or error-laced discovery blob makes an Intel GPU vanish from box['gpus'] with no UNKNOWN entry and no probe.unknown entry, so the planner treats the box as GPU-less.
findings.fix_or_replacement: On decode failure append {'index': int(key.split()[1]), 'error': 'unparseable xpu-smi JSON', ...} or at minimum register it in the unknown list, matching the honest-UNKNOWN contract the file advertises.

findings.title: Record merge overwrites untagged hand fields; 'hand' namespace collision
findings.mechanism: Line 126 compares rec_rank >= rank(h.get('tag')); when the hand dict carries no tag, rank(None) = -1, so ANY probe record overwrites every non-KEEP hand field silently (only a log line). Worse, h.setdefault('hand', {}) collides with an overlay record that legitimately contains a 'hand' key, letting probe data clobber preserved hand values (and lines 132-137 do the same for 'tag'/'src').
findings.fix_or_replacement: Use a reserved key like '__hand__' for preserved values, and require rec_rank > 0 (record must carry READ/MEASURED) before raw-field replacement; refuse to merge overlay keys matching the reserved namespace.

findings.title: kv_line regex loses empty and '='-containing values
findings.mechanism: `re.findall(r'(\w+)=(\S*)', line)` pairs every '=' occurrence left-to-right; a value containing '=' (sysfs path= values, driver names) is split into two bogus keys, and an empty value plus an adjacent key merges tokens. Every parser downstream (parse_dax, parse_nd, parse_drm) inherits the corruption with no validation.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Split on first '=' per whitespace-token: `{p.split('=',1)[0]: p.split('=',1)[1] for p in line.split() if '=' in p}`, and have collect.sh quote or hex-escape '=' in values as it already does for spaces.

findings.title: Cross-check that can never disagree usefully
findings.mechanism: 'image' kinds auto-agree with any probe kind (line 57), mismatches are only recorded in box['probe']['vitals'] and never surfaced in the diff output, and the adapter is wired via `except ImportError: pass` in probe_box (lines 709-716) so its absence or a syntax error is indistinguishable from 'no vitals file'. It verifies nothing and gates nothing.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Delete the module and the probe_box import block; if a vitals disagreement ever matters, print it from diff_box like every other discrepancy.

findings.title: First-match-wins regex ladder over tensor names as the classification engine
findings.mechanism: CLASSES is an ordered 17-regex chain applied to arbitrary upstream naming (GGUF + every HF repo); any new architecture whose tensor names happen to hit 'attn' or 'norm' early (e.g. an expert tensor named 'attn_experts') is silently misclassified into the wrong byte bucket, and the only signal is the 20-name 'unclassified' list which cannot detect misclassification, only non-classification.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Keep the ladder but assert per-model that classified bytes sum to total_gib within epsilon and that expert byte totals reconcile with E x P x bpw sanity (bpw in 1..8); fail loudly (exit nonzero) on unreconciled mass instead of emitting a plausible-looking entry.

findings.title: xpu-smi discovery IDs scraped with grep -oE instead of the JSON it just fetched
findings.mechanism: The script already receives `xpu-smi discovery -j` (machine-readable) but re-extracts device ids with two chained `grep -oE` over the JSON text, then issues one `discovery -d $i -j` per device; a key formatted with different spacing or a new field containing 'device_id' yields wrong or duplicated ids, and N sequential subprocesses (with 20s timeouts each) balloon the probe wall time.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Emit the single discovery -j blob verbatim under its own @@xpu_json section and parse it once in probe_box.py (which already json.loads per-device blobs at line 228); ids come from the parsed structure, one xpu-smi invocation total.

result.shard_summary: A homelab MoE layout planner: a pure-function accuracy/validation core (accuracy.js), a trim/upgrade advisor, a 1100-line no-dependency DOM viz, and a dual Python/JS JSONL run-ledger. Mostly honest, unusually well-commented engineering with real measured-data discipline, but it carries duplicated ledger implementations, O(N^2) stringify/predict recomputation on render paths, a non-atomic ledger seal that duplicates rows on crash, and a synthetic-heat generator whose only tuning parameter is mathematically dead.

module_verdicts.rationale: Dense but coherent pure-function core with real hash-identity, prospective-capture and hindsight-rejection logic; the strongest file in the shard. Needs perf surgery (repeated canonical-JSON digests) and de-brittling of phase-name regexes, not a rewrite.

Structurally sound offline advisor, but bestPassing is executed twice per all() call with full predictRecipe sweeps, and runQuality does per-pair JSON.stringify store comparison over the whole runs array.

A 1100-line single-closure monolith, but a working, accessible, dependency-free UI with consistent escaping. Its disease is recomputation (measuredHere called 3x per render, each re-predicting every run) and full innerHTML teardown per knob toggle — fix with memoization, not a framework rewrite.
A 7-line shim whose only justification is old commands quoted in NOTES.md; the real reader lives in probe/gguf.py. Update the notes, delete the shim.

Small, honestly labeled (ESTIMATE src string) synthetic router whose shape is fitted to three real observations. One real correctness bug: the frac_of parameter algebraically cancels, so it silently does nothing.
Correct but uncached: every rows() call re-reads and re-parses every segment (including gunzip) synchronously; callers invoke it repeatedly per report. Add a mtime-keyed cache.

The authoritative ledger; the pack() seal is non-atomic across the segment-write/replace boundary (duplicate rows on crash), and the whole concept is duplicated in ledger.js — a documented but real split-brain risk.

findings.title: frac_of parameter is mathematically dead in synth_heat
findings.mechanism: C = lambda x: (x * frac_of) ** SHAPE_A / frac_of ** SHAPE_A simplifies to x ** SHAPE_A; frac_of cancels exactly, so callers passing frac_of != 1.0 silently get identical heat to frac_of=1.0. The synthetic distribution never scales with expert availability.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Either delete the parameter (and its callers' arguments) or implement the intended semantics explicitly, e.g. renormalize C over [0, 1/frac_of]: C(x) = min(1, (x*frac_of)**SHAPE_A), with a test asserting frac_of=0.5 differs from 1.0.

findings.title: pack() seal is non-atomic: crash duplicates ledger rows
findings.mechanism: Segments are written and closed (lines 148-151) before the open file is truncated via os.replace (152-155). A crash or power loss between the two leaves the sealed rows present in both a segment and the open file; the next pack re-seals them, and every rows() consumer sees duplicated run ids — poisoning best-run picks, fits and accuracy medians silently.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Write the truncated open file first as path + '.open-tmp', then fsync segments and os.replace the open file in one final step; or record a seal manifest (sealed-through row count) that pack() consults to deduplicate on recovery. Also fsync the segment files and their directory before replace.

findings.title: measuredHere() re-executed 3x per render, each predicting every run
findings.mechanism: frontierSVG (line 238), chartNotes (line 317) and frontierTable (line 884) each call measuredHere(), which filters data.recipes and invokes FM.predictRecipe per row. Every render therefore runs 3x the recipes count of full model predictions; render fires on every knob toggle, theme click and box change.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Compute measuredHere() once in compute() (it only depends on st.box and data.overrides), store on R, and read R.anc from all three call sites. Predictions per run can be memoized by canonical recipe hash.

findings.title: runQuality does O(N^2) JSON.stringify store comparison
findings.mechanism: For every run without an own gate, the runs array is filtered and JSON.stringify((x.recipe||{}).store) is recomputed against every same-model candidate, inside bestPassing which itself runs per run — quadratic stringify churn over the whole ledger on each advisor invocation.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Precompute a Map keyed by model+engine+JSON.stringify(store) -> newest gated run once per bestPassing call (one stringify per run), then do O(1) lookups.

findings.title: all() runs bestPassing twice: duplicate full predict sweeps
findings.mechanism: trimProposals and upgradeAdvice each call bestPassing(data, runs), which re-scans all runs, re-runs runQuality and FM.predictRecipe for each candidate — the entire qualification sweep executes twice per build/report.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Compute bestPassing once in all() and pass its {best, skipped} result into both trimProposals and upgradeAdvice.

findings.title: decisions() recomputes canonical-JSON sha256 digests per member row
findings.mechanism: Inside the per-member loop condition rs.some(...) evaluates sha and digest(core(r.pred.validation)) for every row of the cohort on every member iteration — each digest is a full networkCanonical + JSON.stringify + sha256 of a large cohort object, O(members^2) serializations.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Hoist per-row digests once before the member loop: const digs = rs.map(r => digest(core(r.pred.validation))), then compare digs[i] against v.cohort_sha256 and each other by string equality.

findings.title: Draft/no-draft phase pairing rides on regexes over phase-name strings
findings.mechanism: DRAFT_RX/OFF_RX match substrings like n4/m3/n0 inside free-form phase keys (std-n4, d600_m3_mean); any kit that names a workload containing 'm3' or a width token differently mis-pairs prediction with measurement, silently corrupting every accuracy median built on top.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Make run rows carry explicit machine-readable phase metadata (draft_n per phase) at record time in record_run.py, and have primaryPhase/offOf read that field, keeping the regexes only as a fallback for legacy rows.

findings.title: rows() re-reads and re-gunzips the entire ledger on every call
findings.mechanism: No caching: each rows(file) call synchronously reads all sealed segments (gunzipping the .gz ones), parses every JSONL line, and re-applies the overlay. advisor.js and report tooling call it multiple times per invocation; cost grows linearly with ledger history on every command.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Cache by [file, mtime-of-newest-segment] in module scope (a small Map), invalidating when the open file's mtime changes; the ledger is append-only so this is safe.

findings.title: Full innerHTML teardown and rebinding on every interaction
findings.mechanism: render() rebuilds the entire multi-tab DOM (including both SVG charts, the network table, trust tables with a details-per-run) and re-attaches all listeners via bind() for a single knob change, theme click, or curve select; the 30ms debounce only coalesces knob bursts. All tabs (including hidden ones) pay the cost.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Split render into per-region updaters keyed by what changed (knobs -> chart+layout only; network state -> network section only), or at minimum skip string-building hidden pages and render them lazily on tab switch.

findings.title: Two hand-maintained implementations of the same ledger format
findings.mechanism: ledger.py and ledger.js independently implement segment discovery, gzip handling, the caveats overlay (including the dotted-path recipe patching with subtly different mutation styles) and caveated(); any format evolution (e.g. a new caveat field) must be mirrored in both or JS and Python consumers see different ledgers.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Keep ledger.py as the single owner and have node tooling shell out to `python3 src/ledger.py` once for a JSON dump (offline tooling, latency acceptable), or generate a packed data/ledger.json at build time that ledger.js reads — one parser, one truth.

findings.title: Back-compat shim kept only for commands quoted in NOTES.md
findings.mechanism: The file imports the real reader from probe/gguf.py and dumps it; its sole reason to exist is that old NOTES.md command lines reference it — dead indirection that will drift from the real reader's CLI.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Update NOTES.md command examples to probe/gguf.py and delete this file.

result.shard_summary: A shared browser/node MoE quantization-placement planner: heat normalization, a Lagrangian tier/type solver, and a sprawling 'hard checks' layer that grades recipes by tag-based evidence classes and regex matches over config prose. The solver core (heatSet/prepare/choose/solveLambda/evaluate) is genuinely engineered, but it is buried under a 1500-line checks/prediction tower built on string-key conventions, regex flag sniffing, and duplicated value/provenance lookup pairs that will silently diverge.

module_verdicts.rationale: The solver core (lines 43-670) is structurally sound typed-array math earning its keep; the checks layer (672-1625) is a regex/string-convention band-aid tower that needs a typed facts boundary, not deletion.

findings.title: choose() crashes on empty/infinite option sets (bsel null, option index -1)
findings.mechanism: In the layer-scope branch, if ctx.qList is empty or every base+price cost is Infinity (all tiers capped), `bsel` stays null and line 451 dereferences `bsel[i]`; similarly the per-expert branch can pick `best = -1` when all costs are Infinity, so `add(g, -1)` reads `opts[-1]` -> undefined -> TypeError on O.ti. Capped tiers with cap=0 and price=0 make this reachable, not theoretical.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Guard both loops: if no finite option exists for a group, mark the solution infeasible and skip add() (or fall through to the repair pass); make add() throw on o<0 defensively.

findings.title: Evidence class (seen/inferred/unknown) is tag-table + src-prefix string matching, not verification
findings.mechanism: evidenceOf trusts any object carrying a self-declared `evidence` field outright, else looks up a tag in data.meta.evidence.by_tag, and upgrades a READ tag to 'seen' purely because the src string starts with a listed prefix. Any catalog row tagged MEASURED with a plausibly-prefixed src passes as 'seen'; the whole downstream gateRepair/verdictReady trust chain rests on this string-match rubber stamp.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Make evidence an immutable field stamped at ingest (build.py) from run receipts keyed by run_id, and delete the prefix-matching upgrade path; anything lacking a receipt link is 'unknown' unconditionally.

findings.title: gateRepair is O(N^2) in layer scope and re-sorts ctx.order per pass
findings.mechanism: The while loop (line 856) runs up to N guard iterations; each layer-scope iteration scans all N experts to find the worst 2-bit unit (line 870) and upgrades within it, giving O(L^2 * E) worst case; the expert-scope branch re-sorts a copy of ctx.order (line 860) inside the loop body. For per-expert models with N in the tens of thousands this is a multi-second stall on every render.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Precompute per-layer 2-bit heat once, iterate layers in sorted order of (plan+score)*w heat upgrading until the budget is met — one O(N log N) pass; hoist the expert-scope sort outside the loop (it is order-invariant).

findings.title: fallbackCheck control enforcement is a regex catalog over engine flag strings
findings.mechanism: Controls are applied by new RegExp(c.pattern) against a concatenation of engine_flags/engine_extra/draft_n/isolation prose, then layer-split stage counts are derived by regex-capturing comma lists from the same blob and cross-checked against gpu_split array lengths. The code's own comments concede 'flags are configuration evidence, never proof of executed dispatch', yet the whole control apparatus is built on exactly that string matching — a band-aid tower with no structural mechanism underneath.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Replace the pattern catalog with a single typed `dispatch_manifest` field the engine emits (class -> tier -> proof receipt id); checkRecipe then does exact lookups and the regex catalog, layer_split_pattern, and stage-count heuristics all delete.

findings.title: numaCheck load-extra lookup parses compound string keys ('box|model|engine|banks<=X')
findings.mechanism: Load-extra selection builds prefix strings and parses them back: filter keys startsWith(base + '|banks<='), then +k.split('<=')[1], sorted numerically to find the smallest covering bank size. Key-string encoding of a 4-dimensional lookup is unindexable, unvalidatable, and silently picks the engine fallback when the string arithmetic misses.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Store load_extra as a typed nested structure {box, model, engine, split, banks_max_gib}[] and do an explicit candidate query; delete the string-prefix/split parsing entirely.

findings.title: Triplicated value/provenance lookup pairs (kappaOf/kappaSrc, denseGiBpre/denseSrc, kvGiBpre/kvSrc)
findings.mechanism: Each concept has two hand-maintained implementations — one returning the bare number, one the tagged value — with subtly different fallback orders (kappaOf returns override as raw number, kappaSrc wraps it with a synthetic src; denseSrc drops the bpw scaling branch denseGiBpre applies). Any edit to one ladder silently diverges the planner's arithmetic from the report's provenance, which is exactly how the evidence ledger lies.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Collapse each pair to one function returning the tagged value; derive the plain number via v() at call sites. Three deletions, three survivors.

findings.title: VRAM unit detection by regex against a prose units string, silently defaulting to GiB
findings.mechanism: vramGiB decides MiB-vs-GiB by /MiB\s*\/\s*1000/i on vram.units prose; any other phrasing of the same convention (or a missing units field on MiB data) silently treats MiB figures as GiB, a ~4.8% error that flips borderline vram_peak PASS/FAIL verdicts with no warning emitted.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Require an explicit enum field vram.units: 'gib' | 'mib_1000' and FAIL the inputs check when absent but figures are given; delete the prose regex.

findings.title: solveLambda residual-repair loop is O(groups^2 * opts) worst case
findings.mechanism: The repair while-loop runs up to groups.length times per tier; each iteration rescans all groups from the end to find a candidate (line 500) then scans all opts with a groupHW lookup (line 510). With per-expert grouping (G ~ N/160, hundreds of groups) and multiple overflowing tiers this is a quadratic hot spot inside every lambda solve, which itself runs per plan/score pair per knob change.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Precompute per-tier group lists sorted coldest-first once; repair by popping from the sorted list instead of rescanning, turning the loop into O(groups * opts).

findings.title: expand() packs tier/type indices into Int8Array — silent wrapabove 127
findings.mechanism: tier and type are Int8Array; any model whose planner type set exceeds 127 entries (or a catalog with >127 tiers/mounts) wraps to negative indices, corrupting every downstream evaluate/fill/gateRepair read with no error — the layout simply computes garbage tok/s.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Use Int16Array (or Int32Array) for both arrays; the memory delta is negligible at N sizes in play.

findings.title: layerMap memoization via data._lm mutation with a hand-rolled re-entrancy guard
findings.mechanism: layerMap pre-seeds data._lm[mk] = null 'so a recipe layout below must not read a half-built map', i.e. it defends against its own indirect recursion (layerMap -> recipeDamage -> recipeContext -> prepare -> evaluate -> layerWeights -> layerMap) by publishing a deliberately wrong null mid-computation. Any new call path into this cycle reads a permanently-wrong null that is then cached as final.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Break the cycle structurally: pass the layer weights explicitly into evaluate/prepare as a parameter resolved once at context build, and make layerMap a pure memoized function of (data, mk) with a building flag that throws on re-entry instead of lying.

findings.title: fallbackCheck rebuilds a full planner context() per recipe just to list tier families
findings.mechanism: Line 1489 constructs the entire context (GPU cloning via JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(g)), tier building, fixed-allocation solving inputs) only to extract Set(tier families); checkRecipes calls this per ledger row, and checkRecipe already built an equivalent context at line 1243 — duplicated heavy construction on the report path.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Accept the existing ctx from checkRecipe as a parameter, or extract a cheap tierFamilyList(data, box, eng) helper that reads the catalog without building tiers.

result.shard_summary: model.js lines 2151-4300 are the physics core of a homelab LLM serving planner: dLLM/batched-decode/window cost models, a network recipe gate, predictRecipe tier packing, multi-stage calibration, and discrete-event agent simulators. The modeling is genuinely evidence-tagged and largely non-cosplay, but it is a 5976-line single-file monolith of hand-rolled state folds over untyped dicts, with brute-force grid calibration, triple full predictRecipe passes during fitting, global mutable catalog state mutated mid-fit, and JSON.stringify used as an identity gate (NaN === null passes).

module_verdicts.rationale: The physics, evidence-tagging and validation logic (dllmTerms, winFit/winNnls, agentEngineSim) are real and worth keeping; the rot is architectural density, perf pathologies in the calibration path, and string-based identity gates, all fixable surgically.

findings.title: Identity gate compares canonicalized JSON.stringify; NaN and null are indistinguishable
findings.mechanism: networkCheck and winNetwork establish priced-identity equality via JSON.stringify(networkCanonical(x)). JSON.stringify maps NaN, Infinity and (in arrays) undefined to null, so an identity carrying a NaN rate or a null placeholder stringifies identically to one carrying explicit null; key-order is handled but value-semantics are not. A corrupted or attacker-edited assumption object can pass the identity check and flip prediction from UNMODELLED to PREDICTED.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Write a 10-line typed deepEqual(a,b) that rejects on type mismatch, NaN, and undefined-vs-null; use it for identity comparison and delete networkCanonical/sameValue/ordered JSON plumbing.

findings.title: calibrate brute-force grid: ~311 f-values x PMem grid x models x 36-iter golden, each evaluating every anchor
findings.mechanism: fGrid builds 311 points (0.05..1.6 step 0.005), pGrid up to dozens, and for each combination runs a 36-iteration golden host search per host group, and each host trial recomputes anchorTime over all anchors with fresh anchorParts loops. That is O(311 x |pGrid| x models x 36 x anchors) full model evaluations per box per calibration, and applyCal re-runs calibrate wholesale on every addModels call.
findings.fix_or_replacement: For fixed hosts the f-objective is 1-D and unimodal in log space: nest golden on f (outer) and host h (inner), or do 3-5 rounds of coordinate descent starting from f_default; this is ~1000 evaluations instead of millions with identical optima.

findings.title: applyCal fitting pipeline re-runs predictRecipe over the full recipe ledger three separate times
findings.mechanism: ledgerHosts calls predictRecipe for every clean ledger row; ledgerHops then calls predictRecipe again for the same rows (only differing in the cross_layers filter); ledgerDrafts calls it a third time per draft twin. predictRecipe is a ~260-line tier-packing O(N log N) routine with prefillModel and numaCheck side models, so the calibration path is 3x the necessary cost and the three fits see subtly different data states (host set between passes).
findings.fix_or_replacement: Compute the predictions once into a map keyed by run_id at the top of applyCal, pass it to ledgerHosts/ledgerHops/ledgerDrafts; also merge the three row filters into one pass. Removes two full ledger sweeps and the inter-pass state drift.

findings.title: addModels mutates shared data.models in place and throws mid-loop, leaving half-applied state
findings.mechanism: keys.forEach adds models[k] and injects KLD rows per type as it iterates; if a later key collides, the throw leaves earlier keys permanently in data.models and data.types with UNKNOWN KLD, but applyCal is never run, so subsequent consumers see a catalog with unfitted new models and no error marker.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Validate all keys against data.models first, build a staged copy (models/types patches), then commit atomically, then applyCal; or snapshot data.models keys and roll back in a catch.

findings.title: externalSummary hidden _ext cache via defineProperty is never invalidated
findings.mechanism: Object.defineProperty(data, '_ext', ...) memoizes the external validation summary, but addModels mutates data.models and applyCal refits cal afterward; any predictExternal call path that reads model or calibration state (host terms, borrowHostLists results) after mutation serves the stale summary, silently skewing the external-check percentages printed in evidence rollups.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Make the cache explicit and versioned: store _ext alongside a data._calVersion stamp set by applyCal/addModels, and recompute when the stamp differs; delete the defineProperty trick.

findings.title: batchFit least-squares slope divides by zero variance, propagating NaN into K.row
findings.mechanism: The denominator x.reduce((a,xi)=>a+(xi-mx)**2,0) is 0 when the kernel points share one N (or a single point exists); slope becomes NaN, all three K assignment branches then compare NaN (< 0 false, >= 0 false) and fall to the third branch producing NaN row/fixed, which silently poisons every batchStep prediction built on the fit with no guard or why-message.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Guard: if the denominator is 0 or kp.length < 2, set K = { fixed: my, row: 0 } and push a confounded note into the fit result so downstream tables can show UNKNOWN instead of NaN totals.

findings.title: calibrate temporarily overwrites shared box.pmem.bw; an exception leaves the catalog corrupted
findings.mechanism: The PMem fit loop assigns box.pmem.bw = { v: pb } on the live data.boxes object and restores pmOrig only after both loops complete; any throw inside (bad anchor, NaN in anchorTime) skips the restore, so every later prediction on that build uses a grid-scratch bandwidth value tagged with no evidence, fail-open.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Pass the candidate PMem rate as an explicit parameter through anchorTime (like f and h already are) instead of mutating shared state; the restore block and pmOrig juggling disappear.

findings.title: winComparison parses frontier agents out of a ledger string with /^c[1-9]\d*$/
findings.mechanism: The eligibility gate extracts the captured agent count by regex-matching the prose-shaped marker inside W.frontier.ledger.tps (a string like c16). Any ledger formatting drift (c016, C16, c16x) silently yields captured = null, which degrades every network lever to UNKNOWN for a cosmetic reason, while a matching-but-wrong marker passes the identity check.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Store the captured agent count as a typed integer field on the frontier object at build time (frontier.captured_agents); keep the string only for display. The regex then dies.

findings.title: dllmValidation leave-one-out refits dllmTerms from scratch per row, O(rows^2) over cells
findings.mechanism: Each loo row calls dllmTerms(data, [r.id]) which re-filters, re-groups and re-medians every cell and every kernel-gap group; dllmTerms itself is O(rows x cells). With R fit rows the validation is O(R^2), and each dllmTerms call also re-reads D.fit_modes.v/D.fit_blocks.v per row inside the filter. Tolerable at tiny R, but it is the report hot path and grows quadratically with ledger growth.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Precompute the per-cell and per-group row lists once (grouped index), then each LOO refit is a median-without-one over the affected group only (O(log n) with sorted arrays or a precomputed median pair), turning validation into O(R log R).

findings.title: agentEngineSim event loop rescans every agent and recomputes slot statistics per dt step
findings.mechanism: Each simulation step runs ag.forEach for readiness, slots.filter(s=>s.busy).length inside admit, decs/live filters, and heads.map, all O(n + S) per event; event count scales with turns x agents, so the sim is O(turns x n^2) with a 5e6 guard that converts a large run into a thrown error rather than a slower answer. dt computation also scans all gap agents each step.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Keep a min-heap (or sorted set) of agent ready-times and a busy-slot counter updated incrementally; maintain the decoding set as a counted structure so rate/Dk lookups are O(1). Same sim, O(turns x log n).

result.shard_summary: A 6k-line hand-rolled performance-prediction monolith (roofline/prefill/decode/agent-sim/replica-gate) plus three data-plumbing sidecars. The physics engine is unusually honest about evidence classes and pre-registration, but it is riddled with bisection loops that re-execute the full model thousands of times per report, two competing date-comparison regimes, regex parsing of engine flag strings, and three parallel decode-rate models. priors_adapter.py is pure schema-guessing cosplay.

module_verdicts.rationale: The core (roofline terms, pre-registration records, evidence rollups, replica gate) earns its keep and is honestly tagged, but needs surgical perf and correctness fixes: O(70x-full-model) bisections, string date compare, regex flag parsing, and the hidden __cardFit cache
module_verdicts.salvage_note: rooflinePredict/rooflineScore + rlInstant/rlAfterRecord (5828-5916) is a genuinely good pre-registration boundary worth extracting into its own module

module_verdicts.rationale: Offline report generator, structurally fine, but embeds frozen hardcoded measurements in prose guarded by dead ternaries and re-predicts every recipe at notes time

Walks a self-declared unknown schema, guesses family attribution by substring match on JSON key paths, and rubber-stamps whatever number it finds as PRIOR data — a schema contract, not a walker, is the boundary

Ledger-to-table plumbing is sound (caveat overlay, holdout exclusion enforced), but the served()/draft_twins phase selection is a regex token heuristic tower over free-form phase names that should be a declared field on the ledger row
module_verdicts.salvage_note: decode_fits (228-243) train/holdout overlap guard is worth keeping verbatim

findings.title: rlAttribute bisection re-runs full prefillRoof 70x per term
findings.mechanism: at(id,k) calls prefillRoof (the entire term/pricing pipeline) inside a 70-iteration sqrt bisection, per term, per check row; rooflineChecks triggers this for every non-fit check, so one report is terms x 70 x full-model executions on the hot path
findings.fix_or_replacement: Prefactor prefillRoof into term sums once per query and bisect on the closed-form composition (rlComposedTime already exists and does exactly this on frozen records — reuse it for live attribution instead of re-running the model)

findings.title: rooflineFit: 80-iteration bisection, each pass re-pricing every fit cell
findings.mechanism: at(e) sums prefillRoof over all cells per iteration; 80 iterations per engine per device, and rlEta/rlEtaFor call rooflineFit on every decodeRoof/prefillRoof caller path with no memoization, so batchLandscape and agentLandscape multiply this by 8 batch rows
findings.fix_or_replacement: Cache {engine,device}->eta on the data object like cardConsts does (or an LRU keyed on the fits blob), collapsing repeated fits to one bisection per report run

findings.title: cardCurveFit: 100-iteration bisection x full pipelineRoof per anchor point
findings.mechanism: Each calibration point bisects over pipelineRoof (full multi-stage plan pricing incl. mbHop interpolation) 100 times; with multiple anchors and the rescore pass re-running pipelineRoof twice per point, this is the dominant cost of any multibox report
findings.fix_or_replacement: cardStage is a closed-form of the constants; derive dc/dconstant analytically (or bisect on the per-stage term only) instead of re-walking hops and ceilings 100 times

findings.title: unlockState compares ISO timestamps as raw strings while rlInstant exists
findings.mechanism: String(q.at) < String(u.since) is lexicographic: 2026-10-17T23:00Z vs 2026-10-18T01:00+05:00 compares wrong across offsets, and a zoneless at silently passes; the codebase already has a strict zoned-instant parser (rlInstant, 5829) it refuses to use here — split-brain date semantics in the same file
findings.fix_or_replacement: Use rlInstant on both sides and refuse (fall back to stock) when either lacks a zone, matching the discipline of rlAfterRecord

findings.title: Engine flags parsed by per-call regexes, lastNum evaluated twice
findings.mechanism: cpu_share_re/chunk_re/split_re regexes are re-compiled and re-executed against the flag string inside passTerms (and cpu_share lastNum runs twice back-to-back at 4326), and the same regex matching is re-implemented independently in priorFacts (4555) and cpuPoolCheck (4521) — three regex towers over one flag string
findings.fix_or_replacement: Parse flags once into a typed object (single split on whitespace into a key->value map) at the query boundary and pass the parsed struct to passTerms/cpuPoolCheck/priorFacts

findings.title: kappa bisection over a discontinuous staircase the comments admit fails
findings.mechanism: agentPointRescore bisects decode_step_increment against agentTurnPredict, which counts whole turns — useful(lambda) is a step function, the bisection lands on an edge, the target can sit inside a jump, and the whole fit rests on ONE calibration point which may itself be UNVERIFIED-COUNT; the code papers over this with a nearest-side residual field
findings.fix_or_replacement: Fit lambda by minimizing turn-time error (continuous per-turn timing) instead of useful_tps (staircase), or report the interval [lo,hi] bracket rather than picking one side and calling it FIT

findings.title: Hidden non-enumerable cache bolted onto the shared data object
findings.mechanism: cardConsts defines __cardFit via defineProperty on data so JSON serialisation silently drops it and any clone refits; callers reach the cache only through the mutation side effect, and cardCurveRescore (5283-5284) pokes data.__cardFit directly
findings.fix_or_replacement: Lift the fit cache into an explicit module-level WeakMap keyed on the card_curves object reference — no hidden state on shared data

findings.title: Family attribution by substring match on unknown-schema JSON paths
findings.mechanism: fam_of checks whether the strings glm / v4 / deepseek / ds4 appear anywhere in the key path; a sibling file key like glm_compat or v4_notes silently mis-bins community KLD priors into the wrong model family, and ambiguous paths get assigned to BOTH families — guessed data flows into the quality gate as PRIOR without any schema verification
findings.fix_or_replacement: Require quant-priors.json to declare an explicit schema version and family field per row; refuse (do not apply) on mismatch, deleting the walker

findings.title: Served-phase detection is a regex token heuristic tower over phase names
findings.mechanism: MTP_TOKEN/DSPARK_TOKEN regexes plus _groups means-or-groups fallback plus the lone-token scan in served() (188-203) guess which decode phase was the served width from free-form keys like std-m3/d600_m3_mean; a phase named m3x or m3-final is mis-detected or silently dropped, and the guess=True fallback marks rows as comparisons with no comparator
findings.fix_or_replacement: Add an explicit served_phase (or draft: on/off) field to the ledger row at record time and read it directly; keep the regex path only as a migration shim with a loud warning

findings.title: Frozen hardcoded measurements inside narrative ternaries
findings.mechanism: The glm-lite GPU-cache paragraph hardcodes 37.7 %, 126.57, 22.22, 22.2 as literals inside conditionals that print ? — the prose drifts from data.json on every rebuild while LOOKING data-driven; same pattern for the droopy f refit at 101 and k2e constants at 107-108
findings.fix_or_replacement: Route every number through the tagged-value tables (data.cal / data.bench) that the rest of the file already renders, or move the whole dated narrative block into a versioned changelog data file

result.shard_summary: A genuinely-working homelab measurement pipeline: shell bench sweeps, a canonical hot-expert map format with digests and real validation, an in-engine MoE router tracer, and ledger recorders that cite sources per number. Weak points are cosmetic-but-real: shell pipelines that mask bench exit codes, one whole-file non-atomic ledger rewrite, and a recipe-cloning path that edits serialized flag strings with regex instead of structured state.

module_verdicts.rationale: Minimal, honest sweep harness; only defect is exit-status masking from the un-pipefailed pipeline.
Correct background/wait/rc handling; the fixed-time numastat sample is the only soft spot.
Real canonical format: atomic writes, digest over core fields, validate() recomputes summaries and refuses mismatches. Only edge-case crashes in converters.
Thin, correct wrapper; gate-output discovery and explicit --no-check post-hoc marking are honest.
Real cb_eval instrumentation writing a binary format the Python side parses with magic checks; only fwrite results are unchecked.
22-line one-shot vendored patcher that fails loudly on anchor drift (assert count==1, idempotence check). Does its job.
The --pid /proc/numa_maps path is a real OS-boundary check; the log-regex path is a fallback that its own docstring admits the engine report can game. Keep, but bias to live mode.
Solid ingest with per-model header caching and duplicate-id refusal; reads real GGUF headers over ssh instead of guessing.
Honest post-hoc ingest that marks gaps as stopped/post-hoc rather than fabricating; a few unguarded next()/division paths will crash instead of erroring cleanly.

The 835-line core is mostly sound (per-number source citations, launch vs post-hoc prediction basis, fallback-receipt identity binding), but recipe_from() is a regex surgery tower over serialized flag strings that belongs behind a structured representation.
module_verdicts.salvage_note: recipe_from flag-editing block (lines 660-674): the intent (arm env/flags override base recipe) is right; the mechanism must move to a dict of engine flags serialized once at ledger-write time.

module_verdicts.rationale: Good failure-shape capture with sourced settings; the ledger rewrite is non-atomic and the retry_only definition ignores loop/leak on the retry attempt.
Real monkeypatch instrumentation counting actual router picks pre-masking; only the prefill/decode classification is a size heuristic.

findings.title: Pipeline exit status masked: r captures tail, not the bench
findings.mechanism: `out=$(BENCH ... | tail -n 1); r=$?` records tail exit (always 0) because pipefail is off; a bench that fails after emitting at least one jsonl row is recorded with rc:0 and a stale row, and downstream record_bench trusts r['rc'] as the arm outcome.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Add `set -o pipefail` at the top, or capture via a temp file like bench_numa.sh already does (bench to file, then tail), so r is the bench status.

findings.title: recipe_from edits serialized engine_flags prose with stacked regex subs
findings.mechanism: Engine configuration lives as a formatted string (engine_flags with ;-delimited sections) and arm overrides are applied via re.sub(r'max_tokens \d+'), r'MAX_CONTEXT=\d+', flag-prefix lookahead subs, and label regex surgery (line 654). A base recipe whose label lacks 'at N agents' or whose flag wording differs silently no-ops the substitution, producing a ledger row that claims settings the run never used.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Represent engine flags as an ordered dict in the recipe; apply arm overrides as key assignment; serialize to the display string once at write time. Labels: build from fields, never re.sub.

findings.title: Non-atomic whole-file rewrite of the screening ledger
findings.mechanism: write() opens the ledger with mode 'w' and rewrites old+new rows in place; a crash, full disk, or SIGINT mid-loop truncates runs/screen.jsonl and silently destroys all prior rounds, unlike record_run.append (append-only) and heatmap.write (tmp + os.replace).
findings.fix_or_replacement: Write keep+rows to path+'.tmp', then os.replace onto path; the replace pattern already exists in heatmap.py:71-73.

findings.title: Log-mode verification trusts regex-scraped engine prose the engine itself games
findings.mechanism: The default mode verifies placement against llama_expert_numa_report lines, whose off-target share the file's own docstring (lines 7-9) admits a skewed interleave passes (q4z: 3.26% off yet 121/146 GiB on one node); only the derived per-node even-split comparison catches it, and that assumes exact even interleave. APPLY/POLICY/REPORT regexes are also one log-format tweak from matching nothing, which degrades to status NONE (exit 2), not failure.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Make --pid live numa_maps the default verification path (it already exists at lines 60-78 and measures reality), keeping the log parse only as a NONE-status fallback; fail closed on regex drift by alerting when an apply line appears but no policy/report matches.

findings.title: Kit arm JSON fallback can attribute the previous arm's numbers
findings.mechanism: `js = [j for j in js if j.get('arm') == r.group(1)] or js[-1:]` falls back to the last JSON line seen regardless of which arm emitted it; when an arm prints no JSON of its own, its measured decode_tps/vram come from a different arm's line, poisoning the ledger with cross-attributed numbers and no warning.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Drop the `or js[-1:]` fallback; when no matching JSON exists, record outcome crash with note 'no JSON arm line' instead of borrowing another arm's measurements.

findings.title: Fixed 12s numastat sample misses short arms and dead processes
findings.mechanism: sleep $SAMPLE_S then `numastat -p $pid 2>/dev/null`: if the bench finished (or not yet allocated weights) at t=12s, the sample is empty or pre-load; first-touch arms then feed record_bench an empty node_mib, whose NUMA_FT_SHARE inference (record_bench.py:73) yields an empty mem_nodes list, mislabeling the socket span of the row.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Poll: wait until the bench's RSS exceeds a floor (or 2s ticks up to SAMPLE_S), then sample numastat; verify node_mib non-empty before printing the row or emit a null with an explicit reason field.

findings.title: cli_runs ingest: bare next() StopIteration and unguarded tpf division
findings.mechanism: `i, x = next((...) for ... if CLI_RE.search(s))` raises an uncaught StopIteration when the catalog log lacks the timing line, aborting the whole ingest mid-host; `steps = e['gen_tokens'] / e['tpf']` (line 217) ZeroDivision-errors on a catalog entry with tpf 0. Both crash after partial rows/raw files were already written.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Use next(..., None) and skip the entry with a printed reason; assert e['tpf'] > 0 at catalog load and reject the row with a message.

findings.title: conv_moe_trace unpacks past EOF without bounds check; empty-slice crash in build_map
findings.mechanism: struct.unpack_from('<7i', data, off) and the ids read assume a well-formed tail; a truncated trace raises raw struct.error (not MapError with path context), and build_map line 394 (`next(iter(slices.values()))['counts'][0]`) IndexErrors when a converter legitimately produced zero layers (e.g. imatrix with no *_exps rows), both escaping as tracebacks instead of the file's own error vocabulary.
