findings.fix_or_replacement: Check `off + 28 + 4*n*k <= len(data)` before each unpack and raise MapError('%s: truncated record at byte %d'); guard the experts inference with `if slices and next(iter(slices.values()))['counts']` else raise MapError('no MoE rows found in source').

findings.title: Prefill/decode phase classified by tensor-size threshold
findings.mechanism: `m = 'prefill' if NV.pool.stage_n and s.numel() >= NV.pool.stage_min else 'decode'` — any decode batch at or above stage_min tokens (large speculative windows, batched concurrent requests) is counted as prefill, and a short staged forward as decode; the resulting per-phase counts and meta token totals in route_stats.json are systematically skewed with no flag in the output that classification was heuristic.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Pass the true phase from the caller (run() knows whether it enqueued a prefill chunk or decode step), or at minimum emit the misclassification risk and the count of borderline calls (numel within 2x of stage_min) into meta so downstream maps can carry the caveat.

findings.title: Unchecked fwrite on the trace file silently loses records
findings.mechanism: fwrite return values are ignored; on ENOSPC the tracer keeps 'succeeding' (recs++ counts phantom records) and the heatmap converter then hits bad magic / truncation at the first lost record — all records after the short write are discarded (the converter raises at that byte), losing the tail of every later prompt despite the run completing.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Check both fwrite returns; on failure log LOG_ERR with tr->recs and abort the workload loop (the per-prompt GEN jsonl already exists to salvage completed prompts) — or buffer and write per-prompt atomically after fflush.

result.shard_summary: A reproducible DeepSeek-V4.1-on-RTX-6000 recipe: build scripts pin revisions and verify sha256s genuinely, bench.py measures a live llama-server, and launch.sh is a real tuned launcher — the build/run half is unusually honest. The one rotten tooth is tools/check_atlas.py, a 135-line regex tower that 'verifies' benchmark claims by substring-matching formatted numbers against Markdown prose, which is circular self-confirmation, not verification.

module_verdicts.rationale: Genuine live benchmark client: real HTTP against llama-server, real timings, real draft counters. Only defects are all-or-nothing result persistence and no error handling.
Pinned HF revision + sha256 verification + pinned converter commit; structurally sound. Only unpinned pip deps mar reproducibility.
Dirty-tree guard, SOURCE_SHA pin, packaged libs with hashes — real reproducibility engineering. Unpinned apt cmake is the only drift hole.
Real 800GB pipeline with genuine imatrix binary-format validation and sampled-byte verification. Final hash check for shards 8-10 is displayed but not enforced.
Real tuned launcher, but it mutates global kernel state (numa_balancing, demotion, swap) with no restore path despite its own comment promising one.
String-patching C++ by exact anchors is brittle, but it hard-fails on anchor mismatch and is pinned to one tested commit; should ship as a real .patch file instead.

The whole verification model is wrong: it confirms atlas.json numbers by regex-substring-matching their formatted string inside Markdown sections, i.e. prose agrees with prose. The --accuracy mode is a triple-regex tower over report.js stdout and table cells. Replace with one machine-readable boundary: generate atlas.json and tables from bench.json/data.json so there is nothing to cross-check.
module_verdicts.salvage_note: section() lines 31-44 (heading-scoped fenced-aware section extraction) is a useful 14-line utility if any Markdown-scoped checking survives; belongs in a small mdutil module.

findings.title: Number 'verification' is substring-matching claims against prose that restates them
findings.mechanism: A decode_tps value of 12.69 passes if the literal string '12.69' appears anywhere in the cited section — any coincidental number (a different metric, a hash, a date) satisfies it, and the cited page is itself written by the same pipeline being checked. The docstring admits it cannot catch drift onto another number the section prints. This rubber-stamps self-consistency, not correctness of measurements.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Single source of truth: emit atlas.json result entries directly from bench.json (bench.py output) and recipe-maker data.json via a generator; the checker then compares two structured files field-by-field, and Markdown tables are rendered output, never an oracle.

findings.title: --accuracy is a three-regex tower over stdout prose and Markdown table cells
findings.mechanism: Parses report.js human-readable output by line-prefix filtering, then regex-matches table cells 'P % (N runs, bias B %)' back against those lines with a fourth dynamically-built regex, plus a range-row reconciliation pass. Any formatting change in report.js or the README table silently breaks coverage in both directions, and line 128 `line.match(l).groups() if line.match(l) else (None,0,0)` masks unparseable lines as covered-by-default (b=None never matches, so uncovered — but also never errors on malformed input).
findings.fix_or_replacement: Make report.js --accuracy emit JSON (box, n, median_err, bias); the checker compares JSON to a JSON view of the table parsed once by a real Markdown-table parser (or the table itself is generated from the JSON).

findings.title: Fence stripping and slug() both wrong on ordinary Markdown
findings.mechanism: ```.*?``` non-greedy strip merges across indented/tilded fences and breaks when a fence opens and the closer differs, so headings inside or after odd fences are dropped or invented; slug() does not implement GitHub slugging (unicode kept, duplicate headings get -1 suffixes), so anchors like '#results-1' never resolve and get reported as false misses or false hits on the first duplicate.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Track fence state line-by-line (as section() already does) for anchors() too, and use a GitHub-compatible slugger with duplicate counters.

findings.title: Link scan regex misses titled links and false-positives on code blocks
findings.mechanism: \]\(([^)\s]+)\) skips links with titles `](a.md 'x')` (broken link never caught) and the scan runs on raw text including fenced code blocks, so example links in code are flagged as broken. Same fence bug as anchors(), fixed there but not here.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Strip fences once (shared helper) before scanning; allow `\]\(([^)\s]+)(?:\s+"[^"]*")?\)`.

findings.title: Irreversible global kernel-state mutation with no restore trap
findings.mechanism: Disables numa_balancing, memory demotion, and all swap as root, then `exec`s the server — the comment says 'Restore them afterwards' but the process that knew the prior values is gone. A crashed/killed server leaves the host with swap off and NUMA balancing disabled indefinitely.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Read and save prior values to a state file, install an EXIT/INT/TERM trap in a wrapper that restores them, and exec llama-server from that wrapper.

findings.title: All-or-nothing result persistence across multi-hour runs
findings.mechanism: Results are accumulated in `res` and dumped to bench.json only after every phase completes; with timeout=7200 per request, a single urllib error or Ctrl-C at phase n4b discards hours of measurements. Non-atomic single write can also leave a truncated bench.json.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Write/rewrite bench.json (to a temp file + os.replace) after each request or at least each phase, and wrap post() with a try/except that dumps partial results before re-raising.

findings.title: Final hash verification for shards 8-10 is displayed, not enforced
findings.mechanism: Comment claims shard 10's sha256 equals the source's, but line 76 merely greps SHA256SUMS and prints 'ours:' — no cmp or sha256sum -c runs against the produced store's shards 1-7 or the symlinked 8-10. A corrupted or truncated earlier step passes the script.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Run sha256sum -c against the coldq2k lines of SHA256SUMS over the 7 produced shards and `cmp` shard 10 against its source; exit non-zero on mismatch (document that shards 1-7 only match with the same imatrix).

findings.title: Pinned git SHA, unpinned build toolchain
findings.mechanism: Meticulous commit pinning is defeated by `apt-get install cmake python3` from the rolling ubuntu24.04 repo: a cmake point release with different default flags or a GCC update changes the binary, so SOURCE_SHA no longer implies a reproducible package.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Pin the container digest (IMG@sha256:...) and install a fixed cmake version (e.g. kitware repo or a copied binary), recording tool versions next to SOURCE_SHA.

findings.title: Unpinned pip install into a persistent shared target dir
findings.mechanism: requirements-convert_hf_to_gguf.txt is fetched live and installed unpinned into $OUT/py, which every subsequent run reuses without revalidating; a yanked/changed torch or transformers release silently changes the converter's output GGUF, and the sha-pinned inputs no longer guarantee a pinned artifact.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Hash-pin the requirements (pip freeze to a lockfile committed next to SHA256SUMS) and install to a versioned dir; fail if $OUT/py exists but does not match the lock.

findings.title: Source patching by exact-string anchors instead of a patch file
findings.mechanism: Whitespace-exact anchor matching breaks on any upstream reformat even when the logic is unchanged, and the patch silently becomes a no-op failure at the worst time (imatrix build). It does hard-fail on ambiguous anchors, which keeps it from being theater.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Ship a real unified .patch applied with `patch --fuzz=0 -p1` (fails loudly on drift), or better, upstream the env-var guard into the tier-split branch.

findings.title: Checker executes repo code (build.py, node report.js) as a side effect
findings.mechanism: A script whose job is static validation silently builds data.json by running build.py and then arbitrary node code from recipe-maker; in CI this means a 'check' step is really arbitrary code execution from the tree being checked, blurring the verifier/verified boundary.
findings.fix_or_replacement: Require data.json to exist (fail with a clear message otherwise) and treat report.js output as data consumed via a file, keeping check_atlas.py purely read-and-compare.
